questions.question: What term describes two forces acting on an object that are equal in size but opposite in direction?
options: Balanced forces
Resultant forces
Unbalanced forces
Contact forces

questions.question: How is the resultant force on an object calculated when multiple forces act on it?
options: By multiplying all the forces together
By taking the sum of the forces, accounting for their directions
By dividing the largest force by the smallest force
By ignoring the direction and adding their total values

questions.question: What happens to an object's speed when the forces acting on it are completely balanced?
options: It constantly increases
It decreases to zero immediately
There is no change in speed
It accelerates in the direction of motion

questions.question: How does increasing the resultant force on a given object affect its motion?
options: The change in speed becomes slower
The change in speed becomes greater or faster
The object comes to a sudden permanent stop
The speed remains completely constant

questions.question: Which option best describes the force of friction?
options: A non-contact force pulling objects toward Earth
The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another
A force pushing an object upwards in water
The energy stored inside a moving chemical

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a lubricant between two contacting surfaces?
options: To increase the grip between the surfaces
To reduce the friction force between them
To increase the roughness of the surfaces
To stop the objects from moving past each other

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the size of a force?
options: Thermometer
Balance scale
Newton meter
Measuring cylinder

questions.question: What is the standard unit used to measure force?
options: Joules (J)
Newtons (N)
Kilograms (kg)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: Before taking a measurement with a newton meter when no force is applied, what adjustment must be made?
options: Set the scale to maximum
Adjust the scale to zero
Oil the spring mechanism
Multiply the reading by two

questions.question: What type of variable can take any numerical value along a scale?
options: Categoric variable
Continuous variable
Independent type
Discrete category

questions.question: When should you display your experimental results using a bar chart?
options: When the variable you changed is continuous
When the variable you changed is categoric
When you have no numerical results
When showing changes over continuous time only

questions.question: In a fair test, what should happen to all the variables that are not being tested?
options: They should be changed randomly
They should be kept the same for every measurement
They should be measured on a bar chart
They should be increased after each trial

questions.question: Which statement correctly defines a contact force?
options: It only acts when objects are touching
It can act across a distance without touching
It only exists inside magnets
It destroys energy when objects collide

questions.question: How do non-contact forces differ from contact forces?
options: They only work when surfaces rub together
They can act with or without the objects touching
They always produce friction
They require a lubricant to transfer energy

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A magnetic force pulling metal objects
A contact force pushing against objects moving through liquids or gases
A gravitational store of energy inside gas
An upward force that acts only on solid ground

questions.question: According to the law of conservation of energy, what is true about energy?
options: It can be created when forces are balanced
It can be destroyed by friction
It cannot be created or destroyed
It increases whenever an object speeds up

questions.question: In a force diagram, what feature of a force arrow indicates the size of the force?
options: The color of the arrow
The width of the arrow line
The length of the arrow
The number of arrowheads

questions.question: Compared to a slow-moving object of the same mass, why is a faster-moving object harder to stop?
options: It has smaller contact forces
Its motion is harder to stop because it is faster
It experiences less drag force
Its force arrows are shorter

questions.question: How does an object's mass affect the force required to change its movement?
options: Objects with a greater mass need a greater force to start, stop, or change direction
Objects with a greater mass need less force to stop moving
Mass does not affect the force needed to change motion
Heavier objects change direction automatically without force

questions.question: What is the basic definition of a force?
options: A type of continuous variable
A push or a pull
The rate of chemical energy transfer
The roughness of a surface
